Build a clean minimalist arcade prototype named “Vector Assault.”

Creative target:
- Hybrid of classic Asteroids and modern score-attack arena survival.
- Asteroids is the primary reference for movement feel, fragmentation behavior, panic survival, and vector aesthetics.
- Arena-survival framing is secondary and used for escalating wave pressure and replayability.
- Do NOT turn this into a frictionless twin-stick shooter clone.

Core gameplay:
- Single-screen looping arena.
- Rotate left/right.
- Thrust forward only in facing direction.
- Momentum persists (inertia-based handling).
- Primary weapon fires forward from facing.
- Panic reposition ability inspired by risky hyperspace (cooldown/tradeoff).
- Secondary “Overdrive Burst” with short high-output window and recovery.

Enemy model:
- Asteroid-like hazards drift on vectors.
- Large -> medium -> small fragmentation chain.
- Fragmentation raises local danger and score opportunity.
- Add occasional hunter/ranged saucer-like threats in later waves.
- Approach vectors can originate from any screen edge.
- Use wraparound for ship, hazards, and projectiles unless explicitly justified.

Wave structure:
- Start readable and sparse.
- Escalate with count, speed, fragmentation density, overlap pressure, and special threat frequency.
- Fast transitions, minimal downtime.
- Endless score-attack identity with immediate restart on death.

Combat rules:
- Keep primary fire cadence governed (projectile cap and/or fire timer).
- Avoid unrestricted spam.
- Overdrive Burst is powerful but temporary.
- Score scales with danger (smaller/faster/riskier targets worth more).

HUD:
- Show Score, Lives, Tick/Wave, and pressure indicators.
- Preserve prototype labels when useful: Intensity, Focus, Progress.
- Include actions for Strafe Fire, Reposition, Overdrive Burst, Reset Session.

Visual and audio style:
- White/near-white vector outlines on black.
- Minimal geometric silhouettes, high readability under pressure.
- Avoid texture-heavy visuals and particle clutter.
- Audio should be concise arcade pulse/urgency with crisp fire/impact.

Architecture requirements:
- Follow repository governance and clean layering.
- Domain simulation framework-agnostic and deterministic where practical.
- Keep gameplay logic out of React rendering.
- Separate simulation, input orchestration, and rendering.
- Create reusable primitives for ship/hazards/projectiles/wrap/collision/waves/scoring/cooldowns/HUD.
- Keep constants centralized and tunable.
- Add TODO headers before implementing major new systems.

Acceptance criteria:
- Inertia-first movement feel is obvious.
- Fragmentation materially changes danger.
- Pressure escalates over time.
- Score loop drives replay.
- Restart is immediate.
- Visual clarity holds under high object density.
